data.name: Bawan
data.gender_notes: Bawan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bawan is derived from the Arabic word 'bawan', which means 'blessings'. It symbolizes God's boundless grace and benevolence. The name Bawan carries the meaning “God's Blessings” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bawan usually hope their child will grow to embody god's blessings and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In the Quran, God says, 'And He gave you from all you asked of Him. And if you count the favor of Allah, you will not be able to number it.' (Quran 14:34). Bawan reminds us to be grateful for God's blessings and to use them wisely.
data.etymology: Bawan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Blessings.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bawan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bawan has a significant cultural impact in the Islamic community. It is often used during the annual observance of the Bawan Nights, which is a special time for seeking blessings, forgiveness, and protection from Allah. This tradition is highly regarded in various Islamic cultures, particularly in South Asian countries such as Pakistan, India, and Bangladesh. During this period, people gather together to pray, recite holy verses, and seek spiritual guidance from their spiritual leaders or scholars.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Bawan is deeply rooted in the Islamic faith. It is believed that the month of Shawwal, in which the Bawan Nights fall, is blessed by Allah with his abundant blessings. This belief is derived from the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) tradition of offering extra prayers during this period as a means of seeking Allah's blessings and forgiveness. The name Bawan thus serves as a reminder of the abundance of Allah's blessings, and the importance of seeking His mercy and forgiveness.
